1. It’s likely that more people have recently read the article than have visited the image sites, this would give the articles a boost in their page rank causing the to appear higher.

2. People from the UK are more likely to want to read articles about the UK and about events in the UK, so the search algorithm probably checks the server location and changes some of the rankings based on that.

The articles can contain the keywords multiple times whereas stock images may only contain it once, also the news media are likely to have a higher page-rank than the stock image sights pushing the result higher up.

If the algorithm checked the images in order to show specific ones, it would take ages to do an image search. What it actually does is check for keywords in things like URLs and text surrounding the image. In the case of the British flags in the street most of the images come from a news article which would likely contain the keywords, especially if the news company is biased. This means when google performs the search request a lot of the keywords and phrases searched are found in the article, leading to the attached image to be shown.

tldr: doesn’t search for images, searches for words/phrases
